original_question: Decide whether every numerical semigroup S satisfies Wilf's conjectured inequality e(S)g(S) <= (e(S) - 1)(F(S) + 1), where e(S) is the embedding dimension, g(S) is the genus, and F(S) is the Frobenius number.
target_in_paper: Section 1 ("Notable elements and first problems"), unnumbered statement of Wilf's conjecture: whether every numerical semigroup S satisfies e(S)g(S) ≤ (e(S) - 1)(F(S) + 1). In this paper the Wilf statement is unnumbered and appears on page 15. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's general Wilf-conjecture item itself, not a neighboring variant, and it uses the same inequality together with the same three invariants highlighted in Section 1: embedding dimension, genus, and Frobenius number. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
missing_details: It should define a numerical semigroup explicitly as an additive submonoid S ⊆ N = {0,1,2,...} that contains 0 and has finite complement in N. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
It should define the Frobenius number by F(S) = max(N\S). ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
It should define the genus by g(S) = |N\S|; the paper describes N\S as the set of gaps of S. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
It should define the embedding dimension e(S) as the cardinality of the unique minimal system of generators of S. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, it should make explicit that the quantifier is universal over all numerical semigroups, with no extra restriction to special subclasses such as modular, symmetric, or quotient semigroups. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
refined_question: Does every numerical semigroup S ⊆ N = {0,1,2,...}, meaning every additive submonoid containing 0 with finite complement in N, satisfy Wilf's inequality e(S)g(S) ≤ (e(S) - 1)(F(S) + 1), where F(S) = max(N\S), g(S) = |N\S|, and e(S) is the cardinality of the unique minimal system of generators of S?
justification: The inspected paper is a problem list rather than a theorem paper with numbered conjectures in the Wilf section. The nearest official target to your draft is the unnumbered sentence in Section 1 stating Wilf's conjecture, placed immediately after the paper defines numerical semigroups, embedding dimension, Frobenius number, and genus. Your draft already matches that target essentially verbatim; the only refinements needed are the explicit definitions that make the question self-contained. I did not replace it with the different follow-up question in Section 3 asking whether Wilf-validity passes from a numerical semigroup to its half, because that is a neighboring problem rather than the one your draft states. ([cim.pt](https://www.cim.pt/magazines/bulletin/7/article/65/pdf))
